intervention_label: EUS-guided core biopsy of the recurrent pancreatic body mass, with restaging, paired CLDN18.2 IHC and NGS/ctDNA re-profiling — diagnostic and staging gate
expected_benefit: Establishes four things at once: that the new mass is recurrent PDAC, whether it is metastatic or locally recurrent, whether KRAS G12R and TP53 Y220C persisted through ten cycles of FOLFIRINOX, and what CLDN18.2 looks like on tissue that has actually seen chemotherapy. Four of the eight remaining essential workup items ride on this one specimen.
key_risks: Procedural risk of EUS core sampling (bleeding, post-procedure pancreatitis), compounded by the likely vascular invasion around the mass, which may dictate the route
CLDN18.2 biopsy sensitivity is about 54.6% against a resection standard, so a negative stain on a small core is weak evidence of antigen loss and should not be read as closing the CLDN18.2 axis
Primary-to-recurrence CLDN18.2 concordance runs 83.3%, and the losses cluster in local recurrence, which is exactly this presentation
preference_alignment: matches 'prefers trials, travel acceptable': YES — nearly every trial screen in this dossier needs current tissue, a central IHC read, or a staging call. No toxicity veto or modality constraint engaged.
guideline_status: NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma asks for suspected recurrence to be confirmed by imaging and/or biopsy, tissue confirmation before trial entry, and tumor NGS for every treatment candidate (March 2026 update). Verified against v2.2026 (22 April 2026); v3.2026 has since posted and could not be read.
rationale_summary: All five personas put this first in substance even where they ranked drugs above it: everything known about this tumor comes from a December 2025 resection specimen taken before four more cycles of chemotherapy, from a lesion that is not the one now being treated. The staging read is the load-bearing part. Metastatic versus locally recurrent decides whether the daraxonrasib expanded-access programme and RASolute 303 are open at all, and the ASP2138 monotherapy arms exclude locally advanced unresectable disease. Two blood-draw items ride alongside and need no tissue: the dedicated germline panel NCCN has asked for in every PDAC patient since 2019, and a CTCAE grade for the residual oxaliplatin neuropathy that several protocols cap at grade 1. The sequencing warning the board raised repeatedly belongs here: RASolute 303 requires consent within 6 weeks of the metastatic diagnosis, so site outreach has to be teed up before the pathology result lands, not after.
open_questions: Whether the recurrence is metastatic or locally recurrent — this single call opens or closes the daraxonrasib EAP, RASolute 303, and the ASP2138 monotherapy arms
Whether the archival CLDN18.2 stain (unnamed clone) converts to the 43-14A companion assay, and where a re-stain lands against each sponsor's threshold
Whether a lesion with likely vascular invasion can be sampled safely, and whether ctDNA substitutes if it cannot
The dedicated germline panel and the CTCAE neuropathy grade are separate, parallel gates carried as open questions on the rows they affect
likelihood_of_effect: Diagnostic gate, not a therapy: unlocks four of eight remaining essential workup items and produces the staging call that controls access to rank 2.
toxicity_burden: Low (procedural only — EUS core biopsy: bleeding, post-procedure pancreatitis)
overall: Every option below is scored on a specimen from a different lesion, taken before four more cycles of chemotherapy; this is the step that makes the rest of the page about the tumor actually present.

scenario_label: If the recurrence biopsy confirms recurrent PDAC with the resection-specimen profile intact
intervention_label: Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236, oral pan-RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor) via RASolute 303, the phase 1/2, or the FDA-authorized expanded-access protocol
expected_benefit: In RASolute 302 (n=500, previously treated metastatic PDAC), median OS was 13.2 vs 6.6 months against chemotherapy in the pre-specified RAS G12 population, HR 0.40, P<0.001, with PFS 7.3 vs 3.5 months (HR 0.45). The supporting phase 1/2 gave a second-line ORR of 35% (95% CI 17-56) in 26 RAS G12 patients. Neither number is an allele-level or line-matched estimate for this patient and should not be quoted as her expected survival.
key_risks: Grade >=3 AEs in 61.8% of the daraxonrasib arm (vs 69.6% on chemotherapy), dominated by rash and gastrointestinal events; per-term grade >=3 rates sit in the NEJM full text, which the board read only at abstract level
Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs in 30% of the 168-patient <=300 mg PDAC safety set; TRAE discontinuation 1.2%
First-in-human dosing began in 2022, so there is no follow-up beyond roughly three years and no post-marketing experience anywhere
Oral absorption after pancreatic resection has not been checked in this patient, and no organ-function labs exist since surgery
Taking this first closes the RAS-inhibitor-naive phase 1 doors (KST-6051 among them); AN9025's backfill cohorts are the rare post-pan-RAS(ON) exception
preference_alignment: matches 'prefers trials, travel acceptable': YES — RASolute 303 recruiting, the phase 1/2 open, and an FDA-authorized expanded-access protocol available with drug supplied free of charge. No toxicity veto stated. Oral dosing with rash and GI as the dominant toxicities steers around the ungraded oxaliplatin neuropathy this patient most likely already carries.
guideline_status: Named in no NCCN, ESMO, or ASCO text as of the concensusite's verified read of NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 (22 April 2026). That version went to press before the RASolute 302 publication (23 July 2026) and the July 2026 NDA acceptance, and v3.2026 has since posted behind the paywall unread, so 'no guideline lists this' is accurate as of April 2026 and not a claim about today. The pick rides on the trial-preferred clause for recurrence within 6 months of adjuvant completion.
rationale_summary: Unanimous at rank 1 across all five personas, and the disagreement is about confidence rather than position. Two population mismatches sit underneath the HR 0.40: KRAS G12R was inside a pooled RAS G12 estimand and was never a study population in its own right, and RASolute 302 enrolled patients previously treated for metastatic disease where this patient's only systemic exposure is perioperative and the recurrence is unstaged. Critic and risktaker both argued that these widen the interval rather than lower the point estimate, and the advocate accepted the drop from high to moderate confidence on the record. Risktaker also withdrew the G12R GEMM penetrance argument as an over-correction, since that work describes tumor initiation rather than response to RAS(ON) inhibition. What remains is the only randomized, pre-specified primary endpoint in this dossier that is in PDAC and contains this allele, which is why it outranks everything else even after both discounts. Access is the live problem, not the evidence: the expanded-access protocol and RASolute 303 both require confirmed metastatic disease, and 303 closes 6 weeks after that diagnosis.
open_questions: No allele-resolved efficacy for G12R has been published by anyone, and no G12R-specific arm exists in either RMC-7977 paper
Whether adjuvant FOLFIRINOX with recurrence at 4 months satisfies the expanded-access protocol's prior-line requirement — a sponsor question, not a guideline question
Whether restaging reads metastatic; a locally recurrent call closes both the EAP and RASolute 303 on the same day
RASolute 302 is open-label, so the PFS estimate carries detection-bias risk and the abstract does not say whether reads were blinded
The post-progression plan should be drafted now, since an allele-specific EGFR / RAS-wild-type rebound is already described in preprint
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate: the only RCT-grade PDAC evidence containing this allele (RASolute 302, HR 0.40), read across a pooled estimand and a different line context.
toxicity_burden: High (grade >=3 AEs 61.8%, below the 69.6% chemotherapy comparator: rash, diarrhea, nausea, stomatitis)

counter_productive_moa.description: Pan-RAS inhibition can select RAS-wild-type escape; allele-specific EGFR rebound described in preprint only.

overall: The only option here with randomized survival evidence in PDAC that contains this allele; what is uncertain is the width of the interval, not the position.

scenario_label: If the recurrence biopsy confirms recurrent PDAC with the resection-specimen profile intact
intervention_label: IBI343 (CLDN18.2 antibody-drug conjugate, exatecan payload) via the phase 1 PDAC cohort
expected_benefit: Confirmed ORR 22.7% with DCR 81.8% and median OS 9.1 months in previously treated PDAC selected at CLDN18.2 >=60%, reported as an ASCO 2025 abstract. The dossier's clinical-evidence row records n=83 for that 6 mg/kg population; conservative and critic both read the dose-expansion cohort as 44 patients, and the abstract is not detailed enough to settle which denominator carries the 22.7%. Either way the 9.1-month median does not separate from the 8.8 months (95% CI 6.2-9.7) that a plain gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel class switch produced after FOLFIRINOX failure in the AGEO cohort.
key_risks: Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs 52.6% in the gastric phase 1 (n=116), led by neutrophil decrease 28.4% and white-cell decrease 25.9%, with anemia close behind; TRAE discontinuation 0.9% and no ILD reported
No per-term grade >=3 table has been published for the PDAC cohort; the safety picture is borrowed from gastric
Marrow reserve after ten cycles of FOLFIRINOX is undocumented, and this is a myelosuppressive payload
An exatecan payload arrives after ten irinotecan-containing cycles; topoisomerase-1 cross-resistance in that sequence has no published answer
preference_alignment: matches 'prefers trials, travel acceptable': YES — the phase 1 recruits at US and Australia sites alongside China. No toxicity veto or modality constraint engaged, and nothing here stacks on the neuropathy axis.
guideline_status: No guideline addresses CLDN18.2 in pancreatic cancer at all. NCCN's only CLDN18.2 text sits in Gastric/Esophageal v3.2026 at the >=75% zolbetuximab cutoff. Guideline silence in this framework routes to trial enrollment rather than forbidding the target.
rationale_summary: All five personas ranked this second or third, and the round-2 exchange settled the objection that was supposed to sink it. Critic argued that the efficacy cohort pooled 1+/2+/3+ at >=60% while this report says 2+/3+ in 60%, so the cutoff match was an assumption; risktaker's arithmetic refutes the threshold half, since cells scored 2+/3+ also count at the 1+ tier and 60% at 2+/3+ cannot fall below a >=1+ >=60% line on the same block. Critic conceded that the advocate's confirm-with-the-sponsor framing is closer to right, and what survives is the real risk: a different assay, an unnamed clone on the archival stain, and a recurrence nobody has stained, with concordance at 83.3% and losses clustering in local recurrence. The benchmark objection stands untouched, and it is the reason this sits at rank 3 rather than rank 2: median OS 9.1 months does not separate from the 8.8-month floor a chemotherapy class switch already provides. A topoisomerase payload also does not lean on the checkpoint biology an MSS, TMB-0.83 tumor lacks, which matters in a case where every immune route starts uphill.
open_questions: Where a 60% 2+/3+ archival result lands against the sponsor's central assay on recurrence tissue — the question to ask before anyone books travel
Whether US phase 1 slots exist for a previously treated PDAC patient; the live cohorts have skewed first-line and the registrational phase 3 is mainland China only
Topoisomerase-1 cross-resistance after ten irinotecan-containing cycles
Whether the mOS 12.1 months seen in the 17 patients with a single prior line survives adjustment; at n=17 it is an unadjusted subgroup
Which denominator carries the 22.7% confirmed ORR: the extracted row says n=83, two personas read the expansion cohort as n=44, and the abstract does not settle it
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate-to-low: 22.7% confirmed ORR in expression-selected treated PDAC, but median OS 9.1 months sits inside the 8.8-month chemotherapy class-switch floor.
toxicity_burden: High (grade >=3 TRAEs 52.6% in the gastric cohort: neutropenia 28.4%, leukopenia 25.9%, anemia, thrombocytopenia)

counter_productive_moa.description: Roughly 40% of cells stain antigen-negative; bystander exatecan mitigates but does not erase escape.

overall: The best-evidenced CLDN18.2 route this patient can actually reach, and its own median survival has not yet cleared the chemotherapy floor it would displace.

scenario_label: If the recurrence biopsy confirms recurrent PDAC with the resection-specimen profile intact
intervention_label: ASP2138 (CLDN18.2 x CD3 2+1 bispecific T-cell engager), phase 1 with a dedicated metastatic PDAC cohort
expected_benefit: No PDAC efficacy readout exists. The gastric/GEJ cohort showed a 12-week unconfirmed disease-control rate of 41.7% at >=420 ug, presented at ESMO 2025; the PDAC cohort has contributed safety only. The argument for it is the eligibility gate, a >=1+ central-IHC cutoff this tumor clears threefold, across 46 sites.
key_risks: Cytokine release syndrome in 43.2% of the gastric cohort and 23.4% of the PDAC cohort, with no grade >=3 nausea, vomiting, or gastritis reported on monotherapy
On-target gastric mucosal injury in a patient whose post-resection upper-GI anatomy is nowhere in the record
The monotherapy arms exclude locally advanced unresectable disease, so a locally recurrent staging call closes them
The source is a congress abstract whose identifiers could not be verified against Crossref
preference_alignment: matches 'prefers trials, travel acceptable': YES — 46 sites across the US, Japan, Europe, and Asia, and archival tissue may start the screen while the biopsy is being scheduled. The only friction is the ungraded neuropathy, which several protocols cap at grade 1.
guideline_status: No guideline standing; guideline silence on CLDN18.2 in PDAC routes to trial enrollment.
rationale_summary: Risktaker and advocate both ranked this third and both labelled it honestly as an access-and-fit pick rather than an evidence pick, which is why it carries caveats rather than a clean recommendation. The eligibility case is genuinely the strongest in the CLDN18.2 file: a >=1+ central-IHC gate against a tumor staining 2+/3+ in 60% of cells, a PDAC monotherapy arm with no line limit, and archival tissue accepted to start screening. The evidence case is the weakest of the ranked options, since the only number attached to this drug is a 12-week unconfirmed disease-control rate in a different disease, which the critic called the softest endpoint in the dossier. Risktaker's own mechanistic worry is the one I would carry forward: across syngeneic models, pre-treatment intratumoral T-cell density drove engager response, and PDAC is where that density bottoms out. Ranked below IBI343 because a payload that kills without needing T cells is the safer bet in an MSS, TMB-0.83 tumor.
open_questions: Whether the PDAC expansion is enrolling at a reachable US site and whether archival tissue can start the screen
How the staging call lands; the monotherapy arms need metastatic or locally advanced unresectable disease depending on cohort
Whether any PDAC efficacy readout is close enough to wait for
likelihood_of_effect: Low-to-unknown in PDAC: no efficacy readout in this disease; the gastric signal is a 12-week unconfirmed DCR of 41.7%, the softest endpoint in the file.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (CRS 43.2% gastric / 23.4% PDAC cohort, largely low-grade; nausea 44.7%; on-target gastric mucosal injury)

counter_productive_moa.description: Desmoplastic, T-cell-cold PDAC starves a CD3 engager of the effector density its response depends on.

overall: The widest-open CLDN18.2 door in the file, ranked on eligibility and site count rather than on evidence, in the tumor type where engagers historically struggle most.

intervention_label: Olaparib maintenance, gated on the dedicated germline panel that has not been drawn
expected_benefit: In POLO (n=154, germline BRCA-mutated metastatic PDAC after at least 16 weeks of first-line platinum without progression), PFS was 7.4 vs 3.8 months, HR 0.53. Final OS was null at 19.0 vs 19.2 months, P=0.3487. The honest framing even in a carrier is chemotherapy-free time, not survival gain.
key_risks: Grade >=3 AEs 40% vs 23% on placebo, with 5% discontinuation and no new signals at the final analysis
The strategy presumes a platinum re-challenge that the rest of this dossier argues against
A PALB2-positive result would need an off-label prior-authorization argument rather than a label
preference_alignment: matches 'prefers trials': PARTIAL — this is an approved drug used off-label rather than a trial route, and the patient stated no preference against that. The blood draw behind it costs nothing and conflicts with nothing.
guideline_status: Olaparib maintenance is FDA-approved for germline BRCA-mutated metastatic PDAC. This patient meets neither the germline criterion (unknown) nor the 16-week first-line platinum criterion as written, so any use here is off-label and argued case by case. NCCN has recommended dedicated germline testing for every patient with pancreatic adenocarcinoma since 2019, and that test is still outstanding.
rationale_summary: This row is really about the test behind it, and it sits in this table on the contract's supplementary-key provision rather than because germline BRCA was a feature the user named. Three of five personas never mentioned the germline panel at all; concensusite called that a compliance gap and advocate called it a preference-fit failure, and both are right. The line 'no incidental germline findings' came off a tumor NGS report, which is not built for germline sensitivity, misses large rearrangements, and does not state which homologous-recombination genes were covered. Pre-test probability is low, roughly 5 to 7% for germline BRCA1/2 in unselected PDAC, and recurrence four months after platinum-containing adjuvant therapy lowers it further. What earns the rank is the asymmetry: a blood draw orderable this week gates the only option in this file with an FDA label and a randomized base, and conservative and concensusite both ranked it explicitly to keep the panel from slipping.
open_questions: The germline result itself — the second, unbranched biomarker gate in this case, carried here rather than in the ranking's scenario tags
Whether a new platinum-containing line produces a response long enough to set up maintenance at all
Somatic-only BRCA/PALB2 events and a genomic-instability score, which a germline panel will miss and which ride free on the recurrence NGS
likelihood_of_effect: Low: roughly 5-7% pre-test probability of germline BRCA1/2, a POLO population fit this patient does not currently meet, and PFS-only benefit (HR 0.53).
toxicity_burden: Moderate (grade >=3 AEs 40% vs 23% on placebo: anemia, fatigue, nausea)

counter_productive_moa.description: Recurrence four months after platinum-containing adjuvant therapy argues against the platinum sensitivity this strategy assumes.

overall: Ranked chiefly to force a blood draw NCCN has asked for in every PDAC patient since 2019, which gates the one FDA-labelled biomarker route in this disease.

scenario_label: If the recurrence biopsy confirms recurrent PDAC with the resection-specimen profile intact
intervention_label: ASP5834 (intravenous pan-KRAS inhibitor), first-in-human phase 1
expected_benefit: No published effect size of any kind for this molecule; the second anchor is class-level validation from daraxonrasib, not this drug's data. What it has instead is eligibility fit: the trial names KRAS G12R explicitly, writes down the exact line-counting rule this recurrence satisfies (adjuvant therapy with recurrence inside 6 months counts as the prior line), and accepts locally advanced unresectable as well as metastatic disease.
key_risks: Dose escalation, so early cohorts carry sub-therapeutic-dose risk and dose levels move week to week
No published toxicity profile at any dose
Slot availability at US, Japanese, French, and Spanish sites changes faster than any dossier can track
preference_alignment: matches 'prefers trials, travel acceptable': YES. Intravenous dosing also sidesteps the post-resection oral-absorption question that the undocumented organ function leaves open on daraxonrasib.
guideline_status: No guideline standing; a phase 1 trial route under the trial-preferred clause.
rationale_summary: Only the advocate ranked this, and the reason it stays on the ranked list rather than moving to the surfaced set is narrow and specific: it is the one KRAS-directed door that stays open if restaging reads locally recurrent rather than metastatic, which is the single largest access risk in this case. The daraxonrasib expanded-access protocol and RASolute 303 both close on that call. Ranking it is an eligibility judgment, not an evidence judgment, and I would rather say that than dress a first-in-human escalation in language it has not earned. Where it differs from the Y220C tail picks is that the pan-KRAS class already has clinical validation in this disease and this allele pool, so the class prior is not zero. Sequencing matters: several pan-KRAS trials exclude prior RAS-inhibitor exposure, so this door mostly closes after daraxonrasib, and AN9025's backfill cohorts are the rare exception.
open_questions: Whether the PDAC expansion is open at the current dose level and which US sites are enrolling
Whether the recurrence is documented as locally advanced unresectable or metastatic before screening
Whether the sponsor will accept ctDNA rather than tissue for the KRAS documentation
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown: zero published efficacy for this molecule. Ranked on eligibility fit, as the KRAS route that survives a locally-recurrent staging call.
toxicity_burden: Unknown (first-in-human dose escalation; no published AE table at any dose)

counter_productive_moa.description: Pan-KRAS inhibition can select RAS-wild-type escape; the class resistance map is still being drawn.

overall: Insurance against the largest access risk in this case: it accepts locally advanced unresectable disease, which the daraxonrasib expanded-access protocol and RASolute 303 do not.

scenario_label: If the recurrence biopsy confirms recurrent PDAC with the resection-specimen profile intact
intervention_label: Zolbetuximab (anti-CLDN18.2 monoclonal antibody), off-label in PDAC
expected_benefit: None demonstrated in pancreatic cancer. GLEAM (n=393, zolbetuximab plus gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel) missed its primary OS endpoint at 13.7 vs 13.6 months and exists only as a topline release with nothing posted on ClinicalTrials.gov. The approval rests on gastric/GEJ trials in patients with >=75% of cells at 2+/3+ by the 43-14A companion assay: SPOTLIGHT PFS 10.61 months, GLOW 8.21 months.
key_risks: Grade >=3 TEAEs 87% with mFOLFOX6 and 72.8% with CAPOX in the gastric registrational trials, with nausea and vomiting prominent
Expected payer denial off-label, with a negative randomized PDAC readout to argue against
preference_alignment: matches 'prefers trials': NO — this is off-label prescribing against a negative randomized readout, which is improvisation rather than a trial route.
guideline_status: Approved for CLDN18.2-positive (>=75% at 2+/3+), HER2-negative gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma in the US and EU. No guideline supports its use in PDAC, and this tumor is below the label-defining cutoff.
rationale_summary: No persona ranked this and no persona issued a formal veto, so I am recording the rejection rather than inheriting it. Conservative, risktaker, critic, and concensusite each dismissed it in their notes for the same two reasons, and both hold: 60% at 2+/3+ sits below the >=75% cutoff that defines eligibility under the 43-14A companion assay, and the one randomized CLDN18.2 readout in pancreatic cancer was flat. Keeping it visible as not recommended matters because a US oncologist can mechanically write this prescription today, and the reader should see that the board considered and rejected it rather than never having weighed it. One thing would change the picture: if the 43-14A re-stain comes back at or above 75%, the eligibility half of the objection dissolves, though the GLEAM result does not.
open_questions: Whether a 43-14A companion-assay re-stain lands at or above 75%, which would change the eligibility argument but not the efficacy one
GLEAM cannot be audited by anyone outside the sponsor; there is no publication and nothing posted
likelihood_of_effect: Low: the only randomized CLDN18.2 readout in PDAC was flat at 13.7 vs 13.6 months, and this tumor sits below the label-defining cutoff.
toxicity_burden: High (grade >=3 TEAEs 87% with mFOLFOX6, 72.8% with CAPOX: nausea, vomiting, neutropenia)

counter_productive_moa.description: A naked antibody needs uniform surface antigen; roughly 40% of cells stain negative and there is no payload or crossfire.

overall: Prescribable off-label today and argued against on both counts: 60% is below the companion-diagnostic cutoff, and the randomized PDAC readout was flat.

intervention_label: Single-agent PD-1 blockade (pembrolizumab, MSI-high / TMB-high tumor-agnostic routes)
expected_benefit: None expected. MSS status and a TMB of 0.83 mut/Mb against a 10 mut/Mb threshold close both tumor-agnostic pembrolizumab indications, and neither value sits near enough to the cutoff for platform-to-platform variation to matter.
key_risks: Immune-related toxicity with no plausible offsetting benefit in an MSS, TMB-low tumor
preference_alignment: not applicable — the indication is closed on biomarker before preference enters.
guideline_status: Tumor-agnostic pembrolizumab is approved for MSI-high/dMMR and TMB-high (>=10 mut/Mb) solid tumors. This tumor is neither.
rationale_summary: Carried as a row because the user asked that the MSS and TMB-low result be addressed rather than quietly dropped, and a negative that closes a whole therapeutic class deserves to be visible in the table rather than buried in a caveat. Both values are at decision resolution and need no new order; MMR IHC and a TMB re-read ride free on the recurrence NGS if it happens anyway. The consequence is directional rather than merely restrictive: any immunotherapy interest in this case has to come from mechanisms that manufacture their own T-cell engagement, which is why the CLDN18.2 engager and the mutant-KRAS vaccine routes appear in this table and single-agent checkpoint blockade does not.
open_questions: Neither assay platform was named; TMB from a small panel is not interchangeable across platforms, though that caveat bites near the cutoff rather than an order of magnitude below it
likelihood_of_effect: Low: MSS with TMB 0.83 mut/Mb forecloses both tumor-agnostic indications; single-agent checkpoint blockade has no route in this tumor.
toxicity_burden: Low (immune-related AE profile; academic here, since the indication is closed on biomarker)

counter_productive_moa.description: No target present; FAP+ CAF-driven exclusion keeps single-agent checkpoint blockade inert in MSS PDAC.

overall: Carried so the MSS / TMB-low result is visibly answered: it closes checkpoint monotherapy and routes immune interest to engagers, vaccines, and cell therapy instead.

scenario_label: If the recurrence biopsy confirms recurrent PDAC with the resection-specimen profile intact
intervention_label: JAB-30355 (oral p53 Y220C reactivator), phase 1/2 with US sites
expected_benefit: No published effect size. The public record is a single sponsor statement about a positive efficacy signal at high dose. The eligibility fact is real: US sites recruiting, one prior line required, documented Y220C required, no posted KRAS exclusion.
key_risks: No published AE table at any dose and no posted results
Renal, hepatic, and marrow function unmeasured since resection, so neither side of the risk equation has a number
Dose escalation can assign a sub-therapeutic dose
The class already shows acquired secondary TP53 alterations in cis with Y220C at progression
preference_alignment: matches 'prefers trials, travel acceptable': YES, and it honors the user's instruction that every variant stay on the table. That is what it does; it is not an efficacy claim.
guideline_status: No NCCN, ESMO, or ASCO text names any p53 Y220C reactivator.
rationale_summary: Three personas ranked this and two dissented, and the critic asked that the reason be carried forward rather than smoothed over: the board's tail ranks measure whether a door is open, not whether evidence exists, and they must not be laundered into evidence-backed standing. Y220C fails twice in this patient. PYNNACLE's registrational rezatapopt monotherapy cohort excludes known KRAS single-nucleotide variants, which G12R is, and in the published phase 1 every responder was KRAS wild-type. Mechanistically, restoring p53 function in a KRAS-driven tumor with low mitochondrial apoptotic priming gives cell-cycle arrest rather than cell death. JAB-30355's whole efficacy record is one sponsor phrase about a signal at high dose, with nothing published and nothing posted, which is why it is surfaced with a thin-evidence flag rather than ranked among the live options. Conservative dissented because neither side of the risk equation has a number; concensusite dissented because a zero-data trial slot outranking an unmet guideline mandate is a compliance gap. The screening call is still worth making, and the sponsor should be asked whether KRAS co-mutation affects cohort assignment.
open_questions: Whether the full protocol carries a KRAS exclusion the registry does not post
Whether Y220C persists in the recurrence — ctDNA answers this without a needle
Whether a baseline echo clears the LVEF criterion
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown, and the class points the wrong way: every responder in rezatapopt's phase 1 (n=77) was KRAS wild-type, ORR 30% in that subset against 20% overall.
toxicity_burden: Unknown (no published AE table at any dose; the entire record is one sponsor sentence)

counter_productive_moa.description: Restored p53 in a KRAS-driven, low-priming tumor produces arrest rather than apoptosis.

overall: The only Y220C door this KRAS-co-mutated patient can walk through, and Y220C fails twice here; the rank measures door-openness, not evidence.

scenario_label: If the recurrence biopsy confirms recurrent PDAC with the resection-specimen profile intact
intervention_label: NTS071 (oral p53 Y220C reactivator), phase 1/2 with US sites
key_risks: Not assessable — no published safety data in a population resembling this patient.
preference_alignment: matches 'prefers trials, travel acceptable': not applicable — no reachable route for this patient at present.
rationale_summary: A second US-recruiting Y220C reactivator with no posted KRAS exclusion and an evidence base thinner than JAB-30355's, which is saying something. It is consolidated under the JAB-30355 row rather than scored separately because it shares the same gate, the same class liability, and the same absence of data. Its one distinguishing requirement is that prior-therapy toxicity must have resolved to grade 1 or baseline, which makes the ungraded oxaliplatin neuropathy directly relevant to whether this door is open.
open_questions: Which US site is enrolling and at what dose level
Whether residual grade 2 neuropathy would conflict with the toxicity-resolution criterion
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown: consolidated under the JAB-30355 row, which carries the class read for this patient.
toxicity_burden: Unknown (no published safety data of any kind)

counter_productive_moa.description: Same class liability: restored p53 in a KRAS-driven, low-priming tumor arrests rather than kills.

overall: The second US Y220C door without a posted KRAS exclusion, kept as redundancy if the first one narrows.

intervention_label: Rezatapopt (PC14586, first-in-class p53 Y220C reactivator), PYNNACLE
expected_benefit: ORR 20% across 77 patients with TP53 Y220C-mutated solid tumors, rising to 30% in the KRAS wild-type subset at doses >=1150 mg. No KRAS-mutant responder has been reported, and the phase 1 report as extracted does not give the KRAS-mutant denominator.
key_risks: Nausea 58%, vomiting 44%, blood creatinine increase 39%, fatigue 39%, anemia
On-target acquired resistance through secondary TP53 alterations in cis
preference_alignment: matches 'prefers trials': the trial exists and recruits, but this patient is excluded from the registrational cohort as posted.
rationale_summary: The registrational monotherapy cohort excludes tumors with a known KRAS single-nucleotide variant, so the drug with the only published Y220C efficacy is unavailable to the patient who most obviously fits its target. The published phase 1 makes the same point from the other direction: every responder was KRAS wild-type. PMV runs a case-by-case expanded-access process initiated by the treating physician, so one email is worth sending, but this is surfaced as informational rather than ranked. Serial plasma TP53 sequencing would matter only if this drug were ever started, since acquired secondary alterations in cis with Y220C are detectable before imaging turns.

Critic ranked it third on design strength, then conceded the ranking while defending the evidence read, in their own words that an option with no door occupying rank 3 above a reachable one is a category error. Risktaker and advocate refused to rank it and both left the CARsgen contact in their notes instead; conservative dissented on toxicity, with grade >=3 TEAEs in 87 of 88 treated patients and CRS in 95%; concensusite dissented on the grounds that guideline silence routes you to a reachable trial, not to a closed one. The randomized win is real and it is gastric, open-label, PFS-primary, with about six weeks of absolute gain against physician's choice. The PDAC record is a two-patient research letter, one of whom stained 3+ in 60% of cells, which is an expression match rather than an effect estimate. rationale_summary: This trial arrived after every board position was written and its access verdict arrived later still, so no persona weighed either fact, and I am handling it here. On biology it is the best match in the file: the entry threshold is >=2+ in >=20% of cells and this tumor clears it threefold, and beta crossfire kills antigen-negative neighbours, which makes the 40% of cells that do not stain far less disabling than they are for an antibody, an ADC, or a CAR. On access it fails the same test satri-cel failed. It is a 12-patient investigator-initiated dose escalation at a single Shanghai center, with a companion study at Huashan that is dosimetry-only, and single-center Chinese IITs at this scale have no mechanism for enrolling foreign patients regardless of stated travel willingness. A worldwide registry sweep found exactly three CLDN18.2 radioconjugate studies, all in China, and no Western company with a clinical or declared preclinical program. One event flips this row: a US IND from SmartNuclide, or any Western entrant into the CLDN18.2 radioligand class.

rationale_summary: This row exists because the user asked that every variant stay in scope, and the honest content of that request here is a negative. No approved or late-phase therapy selects on KMT2C status, no trial in this dossier enrolls on it, and the synthetic-lethal hypotheses are preclinical: purine-synthesis blockade in COMPASS-mutant cells, and PARP-inhibitor sensitivity through homologous-recombination disruption, both cross-tumor. The one credible mechanistic paper is gastric and uses double Kmt2c/d knockout plus Pten deletion, which is a long way from a single heterozygous frameshift in a pancreatic tumor. What a biallelic, clonal loss-of-function call would buy is entry to an epigenetic-agent basket trial that accepts COMPASS-complex alterations, if one opens and takes pancreatic patients. Nothing here justifies a separate order or a separate specimen; the characterization rides free on the recurrence NGS.
